stem: A cricket bat is cut at the location of its centre of mass as shown. Then (a) The two pieces will have the same mass (b) The bottom piece will have larger mass (c) The handle piece will have larger mass (d) Mass of handle piece is double the mass of bottom piece

key: 1.8 m from the 2 kg particle, towards the 3 kg particle
stem: Particle of mass 2 kg and 3 kg are separated by 3 m. Locate the centre of mass w.r.t. the 2 kg particle.

Particles of mass 2 kg and 3 kg are fixed at (3, 0, 0) m and (0, 4, 0) m. Where should a third particle be placed so that the centre of mass of the system lies at the origin? Assume mass of the third particle is (i) 5 kg (ii) 10 kg.
Particles of mass 1 kg, 1 kg & 2 kg are placed at (a, 0, 0), (−a, 0, 0) and (0, 2, 0) m. Where should a 4 kg particle be placed so that the centre of mass lies at (0, 0, 2) m?

key: 2R from A (i.e. at the centre B of the middle sphere)
stem: Three identical spheres each of radius 'R' are placed touching each other so that their centres A, B and C lie on a straight line. Find the position of their centre of mass from A.

key: 4.67 × 10 6 m from the centre of the earth
stem: The mass of moon is 0.0123 times the mass of the earth and separation between them is 3.84 × 10 8 m. Determine the location of C.M. as measured from the centre of the earth.

key: (7/12 m, √3/4 m) ≈ (0.583 m, 0.433 m) from the 1 kg corner
stem: Locate the centre of mass of three particles of mass m 1 = 1 kg, m 2 = 2 kg and m 3 = 3 kg at the corners of an equilateral triangle of each side of 1 m, as shown (1 kg at the bottom-left corner, 2 kg at the bottom-right corner, 3 kg at the apex).

For the figure shown, a rod of mass 10 kg (of length 100 cm) with some point masses tied to it at different positions. Find the distance of the point (from A) at which if the rod is picked over a knife edge, it will be in equilibrium about that knife edge. (Along AB: 20 kg at A, 15 kg at 20 cm, 7.5 kg at 70 cm, 5 kg at 85 cm; the segments marked are 20 cm, 50 cm and 15 cm on a 100 cm rod.)

key: d may lie within or outside the body
stem: The centre of mass of a body: (a) lies always at the geometrical centre (b) lies always inside the body (c) lies always outside the body (d) may lie within or outside the body

key: b forces acting on the particles
stem: The centre of mass of a system of particles does not depend on: (a) masses of the particles (b) forces acting on the particles (c) position of the particles (d) relative distances between the particles

key: b is independent of the choice of co-ordinate system
stem: The centre of mass of a body: (a) depends on the choice of co-ordinate system (b) is independent of the choice of co-ordinate system (c) may or may not depend on the choice of co-ordinate system (d) none of these

If the origin of co-ordinate system lies at the centre of mass, the sum of the moments of the masses of the system about the centre of mass: (a) may be greater than zero (b) may be less than zero (c) may be equal to zero (d) is always zero

key: d the geometric centre of the cube
stem: The position of the centre of mass of a cube of uniform density will be at: (a) edge of a cube (b) the centre of one face (c) the centre of the intersection of diagonals of one face (d) the geometric centre of the cube
Three masses are placed on the x−axis : 300 g at origin, 500 g at x = 40 cm and 400 g at x = 70 cm. The distance of the centre of mass from the origin is : (a) 40 cm (b) 45 cm (c) 50 cm (d) 30 cm
The centre of mass of three bodies each of mass 1 kg located at the points (0,0), (3,0) and (0,4) in the XY plane is (a) (4/3, 1) (b) (1/3, 2/3) (c) (1/2, 1/2) (d) (1, 4/3)
A point object of mass m is kept at (a, 0) along x-axis. What mass should be kept at (−3a, 0), so that centre of mass lies at origin? (a) m (b) 2m (c) m/3 (d) 3m

Two bodies of mass 1 kg and 3 kg have position vector î + 2ĵ + k̂ and −3î − 2ĵ + k̂, respectively. The centre of mass of this system has a position vector (a) −î + ĵ + k̂ (b) −2î + 2k̂ (c) −2î − ĵ + k̂ (d) 2î − ĵ − 2k̂

key: c 0.63 Å from the carbon atom
stem: The distance between the carbon atom and the oxygen atom in a carbon monoxide molecule is 1.1 Å. Given, mass of carbon atom is 12 a.m.u. and mass of oxygen atom is 16 a.m.u., calculate the position of the center of mass of the carbon monoxide molecule (a) 6.3 Å from the carbon atom (b) 1 Å from the oxygen atom (c) 0.63 Å from the carbon atom (d) 0.12 Å from the oxygen atom

A system consisting of two masses connected by a massless rod lies along the x-axis. A 0.4 kg mass is at a distance x = 2m while a 0.6 kg mass is at a distance x = 7m. The x-coordinate of the centre of mass is (a) 5 m (b) 3.5 m (c) 4.5 m (d) 4m

Three particle of masses m, m and 4 kg are kept at a verticals of a triangle ABC. Coordinates of A, B and C are (1, 2), (3, 2) and (−2, −2) respectively such that the centre of mass lies at origin. Find the value of mass m (in kg).

The coordinates of a triangle ABC are A(1, 2), B(4, 6) and C(−3, −2). Three particles of masses 1 kg, 2 kg and m kg are placed the vertices of the triangle. If the coordinates of the centre of mass are (3/5, 2), calculate the mass m.

Three point masses m 1 , m 2 and m 3 are placed at the corners of a thin massless rectangular sheet (1.2 m × 1.0 m) as shown. Centre of mass will be located at the point [m 1 = 1.6 kg at A(0, 0), m 2 = 2.0 kg at B(1.2, 0), m 3 = 2.4 kg at C(0, 1.0)] (a) (0.8, 0.6) m (b) (0.6, 0.8) m (c) (0.4, 0.4) m (d) (0.5, 0.6) m

key: a 1 m from O on OE
stem: Masses of 2 kg each are placed at the corners B and A of a rectangular plate ABCD as shown in fig. A mass of 8 kg has to be placed on the plate so that the centre of mass of the system should be at centre O. Then the mass should be placed at [BC = AD = 4 m; F, E are midpoints of AB, CD and G, H are midpoints of AD, BC] (a) 1 m from O on OE (b) 2 m from O on OF (c) 2 m from O on OG (d) 2 m from O on OH

Consider a system of two particles having masses m 1 and m 2 . If the particle of mass m 1 is pushed towards the centre of mass particles through a distance d, by what distance would the particle of mass m 2 move so as to keep the mass centre of particles at the original position? (a) (m 2 /m 1 )d (b) m 1 d/(m 1 + m 2 ) (c) (m 1 /m 2 )d (d) d

The structure of a water molecule is shown in figure. Find the distance of the centre of mass of the molecule from the centre of the oxygen atom. [Each O–H bond is 0.96 × 10 −10 m and the H–O–H angle is 104°]
Particles of 100g, 150g and 200g are at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of side L. The distance from the 150g particle to the centre of mass of the system is (2√7/m)L. Find m?
Masses of 1g, 2g, 3g,…100g are suspended from the 1 cm, 2 cm, 3 cm….100 cm marks of a light metre scale. Find the position of their centre of mass. (a) 67 cm (b) 70 cm (c) 75 cm (d) 80 cm

Particles of masses m, 2m, 3m, … nm grams are placed on the same line at distances l, 2l, 3l, …nl cm from a fixed point. The distance of centre of mass of the particles from the fixed point in centimeter is (2n + 1)l / x, find x ? [Given that, 1 + 4 + 9 …n² = n(n+1)(2n+1)/6]
Find distance of centre of mass of a system consisting of two particles of masses m 1 and m 2 separated by a distance L, apart from m 1 .

If the coordinates of the centre of mass are (7/2, 11/2), and it is also given that point C lies on the line y = x − 4, find the mass m and the coordinates of point C.

Centre of mass of a system of three particles of masses 1 kg, 2 kg and 3 kg is at the point (1m, 2m, 3m) and centre of mass of another group of two particles of masses 2 kg and 3 kg is at point (−1m, 3m, −2m). Where a 5 kg particle should be placed, so that centre of mass of the system of all these six particles shifts to centre of mass of the first system? (a) (1m, −3m, 2m) (b) (3m, 3m, 2m) (c) (−1m, 2m, 3m) (d) (3m, 1m, 8m)

Four particles of masses 2 kg, 3 kg, 5 kg and 8 kg are placed at the four corners of a square of side 2 m. The square lies in the XY-plane with 2 kg at origin and 3 kg on X-axis and 8 kg on Y-axis. Find the position of their centre of mass. (a) (8/9, 13/9) (b) (7/9, 11/9) (c) (11/9, 13/9) (d) (11/9, 8/9)

Four particles of masses m, 2m, 3m and 4m are at the vertices of a parallelogram in x–y plane with one of the adjacent angle 60° and smaller side ‘a’ and larger side 2a. The mass ‘m’ is at the origin and mass 4m on x-axis. The centre of mass of the system is (1.65a, √3a/x), find x.

Three identical spheres each of mass M are placed at the corners of a right angled triangle with mutually perpendicular sides equal to 3 m each. Find the coordinates of the centre of mass. (a) (1/2, √3/6) (b) (7/12, √3/4) (c) (5/12, √3/3) (d) (2/3, √3/5)

The (x, y) coordinates of the centre of mass will be (a) (√3/4 m, 5/12 m) (b) (7/12 m, √3/8 m) (c) (7/12 m, √3/4 m) (d) (√3/8 m, 7/12 m)
